calc.installDetail: Units, currencies and functions need qalc · Enter opens a terminal
settings.styleHelp: qDock's four. Cupertino and Plasma leave the screen as it is behind them.
settings.styleHelpDock: qDock's four; “Like qDock” follows the dock's. Cupertino and Plasma leave the screen as it is behind them.
settings.appsHelp: Apps from Omarchy's launcher, ranked as in its menu.
settings.filesHelp: Files and folders in your home folder, by name, from qSpot's own index.
settings.recentFilesHelp: The files you opened lately, while the field is empty.
settings.calculationsHelp: Arithmetic, units and currencies, with the result on top; Enter copies it.
settings.webSourceHelp: Addresses to open and a search on the web as the last row. Bangs (!yt) work either way.
settings.engineHelp: For the last row. Nothing is sent before Enter.
settings.shortcutsHelp: Your own shortcuts, before DuckDuckGo's: !w Montreal searches Wikipedia. %s in the address is where the terms go; without it, the address opens as is.
settings.shortcutUrlBad: An address starting with https:// or http://.
settings.bangUpdatesHelp: Once a week, qSpot downloads DuckDuckGo's list of bangs, then site icons from DuckDuckGo's icon service: the most used sites, your own shortcuts' sites, and a site you open from a bang. It never depends on what you type. Off, nothing is downloaded.
settings.qalcThere: Installed: units, currencies and functions are worked out by qalc.
settings.qalcMissing: Not installed: qSpot does plain arithmetic. Qalculate adds units, currencies and functions.
settings.currencyUpdatesHelp: Once a day, when qSpot opens, qalc downloads the current rates.
about.description: A Spotlight-style search for Omarchy: apps, files, calculations and the web in one field, with DuckDuckGo's bangs. Nothing you type leaves your computer before Enter.
settings.learnHelp: What you open for what you type comes first next time. Kept on this computer, in ~/.local/state/qspot.
app.running: Open · Enter brings it forward, Shift+Enter opens a new window
settings.windowsHelp: An app already open comes forward instead of opening again (Shift+Enter: a new window), and windows are found by their title.
